title: Arjuna's austerities
hook: in Indra's city, Urvashi comes to Arjuna's door at night, and he covers his eyes

segments.voice: Yesterday Arjuna's austerities ended on the mountain: Shiva healed him and gave him the Pashupata with a warning, and the guardians of the world added their weapons. Did you use only as much of the upper hand as you needed? Day seven hundred eighty-seven.

Arjuna is living in heaven. His brothers are still in the forest, and he is in Indra's city, learning the weapons of the gods. Indra has him learn music and dance as well, from the gandharva Chitrasena. Then one evening Indra notices how Arjuna's eyes follow the apsara Urvashi, and he sends word to her. So that night, dressed for him, she comes to his door. And the archer who stood alone on a mountain and fought a hunter who turned out to be Shiva does something Urvashi doesn't expect. He covers his eyes.
screen: `ARJUNA IN INDRA'S CITY.` → `URVASHI AT THE DOOR.` → `HE COVERS HIS EYES.`

segments.voice: In the telling, Arjuna speaks to her with great respect, and what he says surprises her. You are an elder of my own line, he tells her. Tradition says Urvashi was the mother of an ancestor of the Pandavas' house, so to Arjuna she stands where Kunti stands, or Indra's queen. He looked at her in the hall, he says, the way a child looks at an honored elder. Urvashi answers that the apsaras are free, that rules like his don't bind them. He doesn't move. And she is furious. She curses him: he will live among women as a dancer, without his manhood, and be thought little of. Arjuna goes to Chitrasena, and the story reaches Indra. And here the story turns. Indra isn't angry. He's pleased. He praises Arjuna's self-control, and then he tells him that this curse will serve him. When the brothers must live hidden, unrecognized, he will spend that time as a dancer among women, and no one will look for the great archer there. When that time is over, the curse is over too. So look at what austerity means in this story. On the mountain it was fasting, standing, enduring. Here it's a door, a night, and a no. The same discipline, carried into a palace full of pleasures. The epic doesn't treat the curse as a reward for virtue, exactly. It treats it as something stranger: a wound that becomes a hiding place. And that closes Arjuna's austerities. He went up for weapons. He comes down with weapons, a teacher's music, and a disguise he doesn't know he'll need.
screen: `"YOU ARE AN ELDER OF MY LINE."` · `URVASHI'S CURSE.` · `INDRA: IT WILL HIDE YOU.` · then, large: `AUSTERITY CARRIED INTO A PALACE.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let the breath find its own pace. Sooner or later a small pull may come: to shift, to scratch, to check the time, to think about dinner. If it comes, don't fight it, and don't follow it. Just notice it rise, the way Arjuna noticed the knock at the door, and let it pass like a breath going out. Then come back to the breath. If it comes again, notice again. If you pray, you can offer that small no as part of your prayer. If not, simply let each pull come and go. The bell holds the time.
Arjuna's austerities. They began on a mountain with fasting and ended in a palace with a closed door, and a curse that would one day hide him.
Your line: Arjuna's austerities. Today, when something pulls at you, pause once before you follow it, and see what changes. Day seven hundred eighty-seven.

howItsDone: The episode of Urvashi and Arjuna is told within the Vana Parva of the Mahabharata, and retellers often pair it with the later year in disguise, when the curse becomes Arjuna's cover.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna, a guest in Indra's city. Urvashi comes to your door at night. what do you do?
options: cover your eyes and call her an elder of your own line.
slip away and ask Indra what to do.
fork.reveal: he refuses her with respect, she curses him, and Indra says the curse will become his disguise in the time of hiding.

original.note: Sanskrit Urvashi, the apsara who comes to Arjuna's door in Indra's city.

trapdoor: what you thought: Arjuna's austerities were fasting on a mountain.
what it means: the same restraint follows him into Indra's city, where he refuses Urvashi.
what a scholar hears: the curse is planted here so it can become Arjuna's disguise later in the epic, long before it's needed.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Indralokagamana sections: Arjuna in Indra's city, Chitrasena, Urvashi's curse, Indra's words)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Indra sends Chitrasena to Urvashi after noticing Arjuna's gaze, and that Arjuna covers his eyes when she arrives.
Arjuna's reason (Urvashi as mother of the Puru/Kuru line through Pururavas and Ayus) is softened to 'tradition says ... an ancestor'; confirm phrasing.
Indra limits the curse to the period of hiding; Ganguli gives a length in years. Left without a number under the claims rule.
Assumes days 782–786 covered the departure, the mountain, the Kirata, the Pashupata and arrival in Indra's city; if any of them already told the Urvashi episode, reangle this day.
The practice frames restraint as noticing a pull; no prayer is written.
Editor: review now picks up day 786 (Pashupata, guardians' weapons) and its carry; practice no longer tells the listener what they will want; original changed from tapas (used on day 783) to Urvashi.
Audit: checked against the Vana Parva sequence (Indra notices the gaze, Chitrasena sent, Arjuna covers his eyes, Kunti/Madri/Sachi comparison, the curse, Indra's reassurance); no changes.
